Afrikaans (the language) was considered a Dutch dialect up until the early 20th century, when it became recognised as a distinct language under South African law, alongside Standard Dutch, which it eventually replaced as an official language.

The distinction between Afrikaans and Dutch is bigger than that between British and American English. The words of Afrikaans are very similar to Dutch, but the syntax (word sequence in a sentence) and grammar (flexion of verbs) are different, and occur to me strongly influenced by English (which isn't surprising). Afrikaans and Dutch are mutually intelligible; allegedly it would be somewhat easier for a Dutchman to understand Afrikaans than for an Afrikaner to understand Dutch.

The Danes are Scandinavians. That is another branch of the Germanic family.
